question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹40 and compound interest is ₹41, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years are given, the principal can be calculated directly:

Principal = (SI)² ÷ (4 × Difference)

Difference between CI and SI = 41 − 40 = ₹1

Principal = (40 × 40) ÷ (4 × 1) = 1600 ÷ 4 = 400

**∴ The correct answer is ₹400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (T) = 2 years

Simple Interest (SI) = ₹40

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹41
